channel.title: Paste Media Group - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Paste Media Group (pastemagazine.com)

item.title: Don’t Stop, Girlypop gives the retro FPS an imperfect but stylish makeover
item.description: Don't Stop, Girlypop is a very fast, very pink arena shooter that nails its core feel but misses on enemy design.

item.title: The 21 greatest guitar scenes in film and TV history
item.description: We’re taking stock of our favorite guitar-featuring scenes in film and TV history, including segments from School of Rock, Coco, Stranger Things, and more.

item.title: A24 wins days-long Sundance bidding war for next Olivia Wilde film
item.description: A half-dozen studios were reportedly fighting for the distribution rights to The Invite.

item.title: Rihanna’s ANTI is an elusive, beautiful farewell
item.description: The Barbadian superstar turned her back on the maximalist EDM dance-pop she’d spent her career perfecting, offering instead an eclectic pop deconstruction that voyaged through alt-R&B, trap, and psychedelic soul. As far as farewell notes go, it’s still elusive and beautiful.

item.title: Jason Statham gives his bargain-bin Bourne some heart in Shelter
item.description: The schlocky Shelter sees Jason Statham play a supersoldier thrust back into a life he left behind with an unexpected ward to protect.

item.title: Old school horror and new school survivalism clash in I Hate This Place
item.description: I Hate This Place has quite a few pluses, like its unnerving sound design, but its parts don't come together in a cohesive whole.

item.title: I dream of Cindy Lee
item.description: As Cindy Lee, Patrick Flegel guts his music and yanks out its gooey, timeless innards, singing about love and loneliness and getting “lost in the stars, I’m only flesh and blood” like the gum-chewing dandy he is, twirling gear cables like a lasso.

item.title: Bruce Springsteen shares anti-ICE protest song "Streets Of Minneapolis"
item.description: The Boss dedicates the song to the memories of Alex Pretti and Renee Good.

item.title: Giancarlo Esposito pulls no punches at Sundance: "It's time for a revolution"
item.description: "We have to stand up to it," the Breaking Bad actor declared. "They can’t take us all down."
